7:7.reflection: If God held a plumb line to my life today, where would He find me out of line with His standard?
7:7.action: Pick one habit or relationship this evening and measure it honestly against Scripture, noting one change to make.
7:7.prayer: Lord, You see my life clearly and measure it truly. Do not let me measure myself by comparison with others, but by Your Word. Show me where I am crooked, and give me the courage and grace to be made straight. Through Christ my Lord, Amen.

7:8.devotion: God explains the vision to Amos: He is setting a plumb line in the midst of His people Israel, and He will not pass by them anymore. The era of overlooking sin is ending; judgment will now assess Israel by God's true standard. The verse reminds us that God's patience is real, but it is not indifference to unrepented wrong.
7:8.reflection: Am I mistaking God's patience for approval of things He has already told me to change?
7:8.action: Identify one area where you have delayed obedience, and take the first practical step toward it before the day ends.
7:8.prayer: Patient God, thank You for the time You have given me to turn to You. Keep me from presuming on Your grace. Search me by Your Word, and help me respond to Your conviction now, with a willing and honest heart, rather than delaying. In Jesus' name, Amen.

7:9.devotion: The measured verdict follows: the high places of Isaac and the sanctuaries of Israel, centers of corrupted worship, will become desolate, and judgment will reach the house of Jeroboam. This is ancient covenant judgment announced through a prophet against a nation that had mixed idolatry with the worship of God. It warns that distorted worship cannot stand under God's inspection.
7:9.reflection: Is there anything in my worship or devotion that has become more about habit, image, or comfort than about God Himself?
7:9.action: Examine how you worship this week, and remove or reset one practice that has become empty or distracting.
7:9.prayer: Holy God, You desire worship that is true, not hollow ritual. Examine my heart and my habits, and uproot anything in me that honors You with words while drifting from You in truth. Restore in me a sincere and steadfast devotion. Through Jesus Christ, Amen.

7:10.devotion: When God's message through Amos confronts the establishment, Amaziah the priest of Bethel reports the prophet to King Jeroboam, accusing him of conspiracy. The message about the nation becomes a personal threat to those in power. This verse shows how faithfully delivering God's Word can be mislabeled as rebellion, and it distinguishes between bold prophecy and the political spin placed upon it.
7:10.reflection: When God's Word challenges someone in authority over me, do I humble myself to hear it, or work to silence it?
7:10.action: This week, listen to a biblical teaching that challenges you without immediately defending yourself, and reflect on it in writing.
7:10.prayer: Lord, give me courage to receive Your truth even when it unsettles me, and courage to speak it graciously when You call. Guard me from the instinct to silence conviction instead of obeying it. Make me faithful like Your prophets, trusting You with the outcome. In Jesus' name, Amen.

7:11.devotion: Amaziah, the priest at Bethel, reports Amos's message to King Jeroboam, framing it as conspiracy against the crown. Amos had indeed declared God's judgment: the king would fall and Israel would go into exile. The priest hears God's warning only as political trouble, not as a call to repent.
7:11.reflection: When a hard message from God reaches me, do I treat it as a threat to my comfort or as an invitation to return to Him?
7:11.action: Recall one correction or warning you have recently brushed aside, and spend five minutes today honestly bringing it to God in prayer.
7:11.prayer: Lord, give me ears that hear even when Your word unsettles me. Keep me from shooting the messenger or silencing the truth. Soften my heart, that Your warnings would lead me to repentance rather than resistance. In Jesus' name, amen.

7:12.devotion: Amaziah tells Amos to flee to Judah and earn his bread there, implying prophets prophesy for profit and that Bethel is no place for such messages. He reduces a word from the Lord to an unwelcome profession, hoping geography can silence it.
7:12.reflection: Have I ever tried to move an inconvenient truth out of my life instead of letting it change me?
7:12.action: Identify one truth of Scripture you have been avoiding, and read a passage about it today instead of turning away.
7:12.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times I have tried to relocate Your truth rather than receive it. Give me courage to welcome Your word into every corner of my life, even the places I would rather keep off-limits. Amen.

7:13.devotion: Amaziah forbids Amos to prophesy at Bethel, calling it the king's sanctuary and royal residence. What had begun as a place of seeking God has become defined by power and politics. Authority is being used to shut out the voice of the Lord.
7:13.reflection: Where might loyalty to an institution, leader, or habit be quietly outranking my loyalty to God's word?
7:13.action: Write down one area where you follow human approval more readily than God's truth, and name it honestly before Him today.
7:13.prayer: Lord, You are greater than every throne and every institution. Guard me from letting any human authority, including my own preferences, silence Your voice. Help me honor leaders rightly while keeping You first. Through Christ, amen.

7:14.devotion: Amos answers that he was no professional prophet, nor from a prophetic family; he was a sheepbreeder and tender of sycamore trees. God's message did not come through credentials or career, and Amos does not defend himself but points away from himself to his calling.
7:14.reflection: Am I ever tempted to think God cannot use me because I lack the right background, training, or title?
7:14.action: Offer God one ordinary skill or responsibility from your daily life today, asking Him to use it for His purposes.
7:14.prayer: Gracious God, thank You that You call ordinary people to carry Your word. Free me from feeling unqualified, and from boasting when I am qualified. Use my plain, everyday life to serve You faithfully. In Jesus' name, amen.

7:15.devotion: Amos testifies that the Lord took him as he followed the flock and told him to go prophesy to God's people Israel. His calling was entirely God's initiative. The same Lord who sent him to uncomfortable work remains the true source of every message he speaks.
7:15.reflection: Am I listening for God's call, or only assuming He would never ask anything surprising of me?
7:15.action: Set aside ten quiet minutes today to pray about where God may be calling you to serve, and write down what comes to mind.
7:15.prayer: Lord, You took Amos from the fields and sent him with Your word. Take my life as it is and send me where You will. Give me courage to obey when Your call stretches me beyond my plans. Amen.

7:16.devotion: Amos turns from defending himself to delivering God's reply. Amaziah had commanded, in effect, that no hard word be spoken against Israel. But Amos refuses to soften it, because silencing the message would serve neither the priest nor the people.
7:16.reflection: When God's word confronts me, do I want it explained away, or do I want to be changed?
7:16.action: Choose one verse that challenges you and read it slowly today, asking God to apply it rather than soften it.
7:16.prayer: Father, keep me from curating Your word to suit my tastes. When it speaks against my sin, give me humility to listen and strength to change. Thank You that Your truth is always meant for my good. In Christ, amen.

7:17.devotion: God announces the personal consequences of Amaziah's opposition: his family and land would suffer as Israel goes into exile. This is sobering ancient judgment narrative, showing that rejecting God's warning did not shield the priest from the coming disaster. It calls us to heed God rather than resist Him, and to trust His justice rather than repeat violence ourselves.
7:17.reflection: If pride is hardening me against God's correction, what might it be costing me that I have not yet noticed?
7:17.action: Pray today for a soft heart toward God's correction, and ask one trusted friend to speak honestly with you about your spiritual life.
7:17.prayer: Righteous Lord, Your judgments are true, and Your warnings are mercy before disaster falls. Keep me from hardening my heart against You. Teach me to receive correction with humility and to trust Your justice. In Jesus' name, amen.

8:1.devotion: God shows Amos a vision: a basket of summer fruit. In this opening of a new section, the ordinary image becomes a prophetic sign. Just as ripe fruit signals the end of a season, it pointed Israel toward the ripeness of their time—judgment was near, and the moment for repentance was running out.
8:1.reflection: If God were to show me the state of my life in one ordinary picture today, what would it reveal about my season?
8:1.action: Notice one ordinary object today—a fruit, a clock, a basket—and let it prompt a brief prayer about how you are using your time.
8:1.prayer: Lord, You speak through simple things, and You give us time now to turn to You. Wake me from delay and complacency. Help me treat today as the season for seeking You, not tomorrow. In Jesus' name, amen.

8:2.devotion: God shows Amos a basket of summer fruit, a vivid picture of ripeness: just as ripe fruit is ready to be consumed, Israel is ripe for judgment. The wordplay in Hebrew links fruit to end. God's patient forbearance with His people's persistent unfaithfulness has reached its appointed limit.
8:2.reflection: If God examined the fruit of my life right now, would it be ripe with faithfulness or spoiled by neglect?
8:2.action: Set aside ten minutes today to honestly inventory one habit or pattern that has been quietly ripening toward trouble, and write it down.
8:2.prayer: Lord, thank You for Your patience with me. Open my eyes to see myself honestly as You see me. Before any warning becomes final, turn my heart back to You in genuine repentance. Amen.

8:3.devotion: Amos foresees a day when temple songs of celebration will turn into wailing. Judgment will fall so heavily that many bodies lie everywhere, and the people will be too stunned even to mourn properly. This sobering ancient oracle shows that hollow worship cannot shield a nation from the consequences of persistent injustice.
8:3.reflection: Is my worship a true expression of a life that honors God, or a cover for habits He has been warning me about?
8:3.action: Before your next time of worship, pause and ask God to search your heart, confessing anything you have been hiding behind religious routine.
8:3.prayer: Father, I do not want my songs to be empty noise. Let my worship rise from an honest and obedient heart. Have mercy on me, and draw me into worship that matches my daily walk with You. Amen.

8:4.devotion: God turns His word directly against those who exploit the needy and crush the poor of the land. In Israel, prosperity had been built on trampling the vulnerable. Scripture consistently shows that God takes the treatment of the poor personally; how a society treats its weakest members reveals its true standing before Him.
8:4.reflection: Whose vulnerability am I tempted to overlook or take advantage of when it benefits me?
8:4.action: Identify one person in your community who is struggling financially or socially, and do one practical kindness for them today.
8:4.prayer: Lord, You see every person the world overlooks. Forgive me for the times I have ignored the needy or acted in self-interest. Give me Your compassion and make me an agent of justice and mercy. Amen.

8:5.devotion: Amos exposes the merchants who keep religious feasts outwardly but grumble that the holy days end so they can resume trading. Their business practices cheat customers: shrinking measures, inflating prices, and falsifying scales. Worship and dishonest commerce sat side by side, and God refuses to accept that divide.
8:5.reflection: Where do I quietly compromise honesty in work, money, or dealings with others while still calling myself a person of faith?
8:5.action: Review one area of your finances or work practices today and correct any exaggeration, dishonest claim, or unfair dealing you find.
8:5.prayer: God of truth, You hate deceit even in small things. Show me where my practices do not match my profession of faith. Give me integrity in every transaction, so my whole life honors You. Amen.

8:6.devotion: The corrupt merchants treat people like merchandise, buying the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and even sell adulterated grain. Human beings made in God's image are reduced to profit. Amos reminds every generation that exploiting people for gain invites God's certain opposition.
8:6.reflection: Do I ever treat people as tools for my benefit rather than as persons God loves and values?
8:6.action: Choose one relationship where convenience has replaced genuine care, and invest real time in that person today without asking for anything in return.
8:6.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times I have valued things over people. Remind me that every person I meet bears Your image. Make me generous, fair, and tender toward those who can offer me nothing. Amen.

8:7.devotion: The LORD swears an oath concerning Israel's sins: He will never forget any of their works. This is not a vindictive forgetting of repentant people but a declaration that unrepented exploitation is permanently on record before Him. God's justice is not forgetful or casual; every act of oppression matters to Him.
8:7.reflection: What do I assume God has overlooked that I have never actually brought to Him in repentance?
8:7.action: Name one unresolved sin before God today in prayer, confess it plainly, and take one step of restitution if someone was harmed.
8:7.prayer: Righteous Lord, nothing is hidden from You. Thank You that honest confession meets Your mercy in Christ. I bring my hidden wrongs into Your light today, trusting Your forgiveness and asking grace to make things right. Amen.

8:8.devotion: Amos asks whether the land itself should not tremble because of such injustice, rising and subsiding like the flooding Nile. Covenant unfaithfulness affects the whole community, not only the wrongdoers. Sin against the vulnerable was never a private matter in Israel; it brought grief and upheaval on everyone who dwelt there.
8:8.reflection: Am I willing to admit that unaddressed wrongdoing affects not just me but everyone connected to my life?
8:8.action: Consider one way your choices affect your household, workplace, or church, and make one change today that blesses rather than burdens those around you.
8:8.prayer: Lord, You remind me that no one sins alone. Use my life as a source of peace and healing in my community, not unrest. Teach me to weigh my actions by their effect on others. Amen.

8:9.devotion: God declares that on the day of judgment the sun will go down at noon and darkness will fall in broad daylight. This striking image conveys that the day of the Lord will upend every expectation, turning apparent security into sudden gloom. For those who lived complacently, light would give way to darkness without warning.
8:9.reflection: If darkness suddenly interrupted the bright routine of my life today, what would I find my security was actually built on?
8:9.action: Write down where your sense of security truly rests, then pray over that list, surrendering each item to God's trustworthy care.
8:9.prayer: Father, I confess how easily I trust in bright circumstances rather than in You. Anchor my security in Your unchanging faithfulness, so that whether days are light or dark, my hope stands firm in You. Amen.

8:10.devotion: Amos delivered God's word to Israel during prosperity, warning that complacent celebration would give way to grief. Because the people ignored injustice and neglected God, their festivals would end in mourning like the loss of an only son—a sober picture of how sin hollows out even joyful seasons.
8:10.reflection: Have I let comfort dull my sensitivity to God's heart for justice and worship?
8:10.action: Examine one routine celebration or habit today, and honestly ask God to reveal anything in it that has crowded Him out.
8:10.prayer: Lord, keep my joy rooted in You rather than in comfort. Wake me from spiritual complacency, and let my celebrations honor You with a heart that grieves what grieves You. Amen.

8:11.devotion: At the climax of Amos's vision, God warns of a famine worse than hunger: silence from heaven. Israel, who ignored the prophets' words, would one day desperately long to hear the LORD and find no word. The passage warns against treating God's voice as ordinary or disposable.
8:11.reflection: Do I treasure Scripture as bread for my soul, or have I grown numb to its voice?
8:11.action: Set aside fifteen minutes today to read the Bible slowly, thanking God for the privilege of hearing His word so freely.
8:11.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times Your word felt like background noise. Feed me through Scripture today, and give me a hunger that treasures every word You speak. Amen.

8:12.devotion: Amos pictures people wandering from sea to sea, running north and east, searching for the word of the LORD and not finding it. What they once had in abundance and ignored became unavailable. This warns that spiritual opportunities neglected can fade, and God's word is worth seeking while it may be heard.
8:12.reflection: Am I treating God's word as urgent treasure, or postponing it as if it will always be there?
8:12.action: Before bed tonight, recall one Scripture from this week and write down how it spoke to your situation.
8:12.prayer: Lord, You are not far from any who seek You. Keep me running toward Your word daily, not wandering in neglect. Anchor my heart in the Scripture You have so graciously given. Amen.

8:13.devotion: Amos describes even the strongest and most promising of the young fainting with thirst in that day of judgment. The verse shows that youth, strength, and beauty cannot sustain a soul deprived of God's word. Human vitality fails where the Spirit's refreshment is absent.
8:13.reflection: On what am I leaning for strength—my own vigor and resources, or the living word of God?
8:13.action: Identify one area where you have been relying on your own strength, and intentionally pray about it before acting today.
8:13.prayer: Father, my strength has limits, but Your word does not. Satisfy my thirst with Your presence, and teach me to depend on You rather than on my own youth, energy, or ability. Amen.

8:14.devotion: Amos condemns those who swore by idols at Samaria, Dan, and Beersheba—shrines associated with false worship. Trusting gods that cannot save, they would fall and not rise. The passage warns that misplaced worship leads to collapse, and only the living God sustains His people.
8:14.reflection: What modern substitute for God am I tempted to swear by—money, success, image, or approval?
8:14.action: Name one false source of security you have been trusting, and take a practical step to loosen its grip, such as giving, simplifying, or confessing it to a friend.
8:14.prayer: Living God, expose the idols I prop up in place of You. Forgive my misplaced trust, and re-center my worship on You alone, the only One who truly holds me up. Amen.

9:1.devotion: Amos sees the Lord standing by the altar, commanding judgment to strike the temple. Nowhere in the sanctuary—no altar, no threshold—could shelter those who had corrupted worship and oppressed the poor. The vision teaches that God's holiness confronts sin even in sacred places.
9:1.reflection: Do I approach worship with reverence for God's holiness, or has it become mere routine?
9:1.action: Before your next worship time, pause for a moment of silence, asking God to search your heart and prepare you to meet Him honestly.
9:1.prayer: Holy God, You see me truly, even in sacred moments. Strip away pretense in my worship. Meet me with Your holiness and mercy, and make my reverence for You genuine and whole. Amen.

9:2.devotion: God declares that no depth or height can hide the unrepentant from His judgment—if they dig into the grave or climb to heaven, His hand reaches them. This is a warning to those fleeing God, yet Scripture elsewhere shows this same reach bringing grace to those who seek Him.
9:2.reflection: Am I hiding from God about something, believing He does not see or care?
9:2.action: Bring to God today, in honest prayer, one thing you have been hiding or avoiding, and ask for His mercy rather than continuing to conceal it.
9:2.prayer: Father, You see every depth and height of my life. I stop hiding. Meet me in the open with Your mercy, forgive what I have concealed, and lead me into honest fellowship with You. Amen.

9:3.devotion: Amos continues the vision: even hiding atop Mount Carmel or at the bottom of the sea cannot shield the unrepentant from God. The imagery proclaims His absolute sovereignty over every place—mountain, sea, and all between. For the repentant heart, this same all-seeing God is a refuge, not a threat.
9:3.reflection: Do I experience God's everywhere-presence as a comfort, or does it make me want to hide?
9:3.action: Choose one hidden corner of your life—a habit, worry, or memory—and invite God's light into it through a written prayer today.
9:3.prayer: Lord of mountain and sea, nothing is beyond Your reach. Since You see me fully, let me not run but rest in You. Turn Your searching gaze into comfort as I walk openly with You today. Amen.

9:4.devotion: Amos concludes his message of coming judgment on unrepentant Israel. Even if the people flee into exile before their enemies, God declares that no hiding place will shield them from the consequences of persistent rebellion. This sober word reminds us that God's justice cannot be escaped by distance or disguise.
9:4.reflection: Am I trying to outrun God's conviction in some area of my life instead of turning back to Him?
9:4.action: Identify one sin you have been avoiding or excusing, and confess it honestly to God in prayer today.
9:4.prayer: Lord, You see everything, even the places I try to hide. Stop my fleeing heart and turn me toward You. Bring me to honest repentance, not because I dread Your judgment alone, but because I long for Your presence and mercy.

9:5.devotion: Amos describes the awe-inspiring power of the Lord GOD of hosts. At His touch the earth melts and its inhabitants mourn, and the land rises and falls like the Nile's waters. The verse grounds Israel's coming judgment in the majesty of the God who governs all creation.
9:5.reflection: Do I approach God with a real sense of His majesty and power, or have I grown casual in His presence?
9:5.action: Spend five quiet minutes today simply contemplating God's greatness in creation before bringing Him any requests.
9:5.prayer: Almighty God, You touch the earth and it melts; the whole creation trembles before You. Teach me to hold You in proper awe. May reverence for Your power shape the way I worship, obey, and trust You each day.

9:6.devotion: Amos continues describing God's sovereign greatness: He builds His chambers in the heavens, foundations in the earth, and commands the waters of the sea, pouring them upon the land. The LORD's name seals this confession. The God who judges is the same God who orders and sustains the world.
9:6.reflection: How does remembering that God sustains heaven and earth change the way I view my own troubles today?
9:6.action: When a worry arises today, pause and name aloud that the Lord who rules the seas also rules that situation.
9:6.prayer: LORD, You built the heights of heaven and founded the earth, and the seas obey Your call. Help me rest in Your sovereignty over every detail of my life. You are great, and You are good, and You are near.

9:7.devotion: God challenges Israel's false security as His favored people. He reminds them that He has guided other nations too—the Philistines from Caphtor and the Syrians from Kir—just as He brought Israel from Egypt. Election carries responsibility; it is never a license for presumption or complacency.
9:7.reflection: Have I begun to assume God's favor while ignoring His call to live obediently and justly?
9:7.action: Thank God for one way He has worked in your life, then ask Him what obedience He is calling for in response.
9:7.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times I have taken Your grace for granted. You are Lord over all peoples and all histories. Keep me humble, grateful, and obedient, that I may live as one who truly knows Your mercy.

9:8.devotion: God's eyes are fixed on the sinful kingdom, and He promises its destruction—yet He declares He will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob. Judgment falls on persistent sin, but a remnant of mercy remains. Even in severe discipline, God preserves a people for Himself.
9:8.reflection: Where do I need to trust that God's discipline, though painful, is never His final word for those who belong to Him?
9:8.action: Write down one current hardship and beside it note how God might be refining rather than abandoning you.
9:8.prayer: Righteous God, You take sin seriously, and I must not minimize mine. Yet thank You that Your mercy spares a remnant and preserves Your people. In seasons of correction, hold me fast and teach me all You intend me to learn.

9:9.devotion: God promises to sift the house of Israel among the nations like grain in a sieve, yet not the smallest grain will fall to the ground. The sifting separates sinners from the faithful. It is an image of painful refinement, but also of careful preservation—God loses none who are His.
9:9.reflection: When life shakes me, do I trust that God is refining me and holding onto me, even in the turmoil?
9:9.action: Memorize the phrase 'not the smallest grain shall fall to the ground' and recall it when you feel shaken today.
9:9.prayer: Lord, the siftings of life are hard, and I do not always understand them. Thank You that Your hand is precise and careful, and that nothing of true worth is lost. Refine my faith and keep me secure in You.

9:10.devotion: Amos exposes the false confidence of sinners among God's people who dismiss warnings, saying calamity will never overtake them. Such security, built on denial rather than repentance, invites judgment. This verse warns against comfortable complacency and against silencing the honest voice of conviction.
9:10.reflection: Have I been telling myself that consequences will never come, instead of responding honestly to God's warnings?
9:10.action: Name one warning from Scripture you have been ignoring, and take one step of obedience toward it today.
9:10.prayer: Father, deliver me from false peace that ignores Your truth. Keep me from saying 'it will never happen to me' when You are calling me to repent. Give me a soft heart that hears Your warnings and turns to You promptly.

9:11.devotion: After words of judgment, God promises restoration: He will raise up the fallen tabernacle of David, repair its breaches, rebuild its ruins, and restore it as in days of old. This hopeful promise of a renewed Davidic kingdom points to God's faithfulness beyond discipline and, in the New Testament, to the coming of Christ.
9:11.reflection: Where in my life do I need to hope that God can rebuild what has fallen down?
9:11.action: Choose one broken or neglected area of your life and take one small, concrete step of repair or restoration today.
9:11.prayer: Faithful God, You promise to raise what has fallen and repair what is ruined. Thank You that Your plans do not end in wreckage but in restoration, fulfilled in Jesus. Rebuild the broken places in my life and let me hope in You.

9:12.devotion: At the close of Amos, judgment gives way to hope. God promises to restore David's fallen house so that His people will encompass even Edom, Israel's old enemy, and all the Gentiles called by His name. What began as a word of doom ends with a vision of worldwide belonging under the Lord who does this thing.
9:12.reflection: Who do I consider outside the reach of God's mercy, and could they actually be included in His family?
9:12.action: Pray by name today for someone from a different background or faith, asking God to draw them to Himself.
9:12.prayer: Lord, Your plan is wider than my imagination. Thank You that people from every nation are called by Your name. Widen my heart to welcome those I would exclude, and make me a witness of Your restoring grace. Amen.

9:13.devotion: God paints restoration as breathtaking abundance: harvests so plentiful that planting and reaping overlap, and vineyards heavy with wine flowing down the hills. For farmers who endured plague, locusts, and drought in Amos's day, this image promised that God's renewing work would overflow beyond every normal season.
9:13.reflection: Where in my life am I living from scarcity, forgetting the generous God who restores what has been lost?
9:13.action: Notice one area of God's provision today and share something from it generously with another person.
9:13.prayer: Generous God, You delight to restore overflowing. Forgive my stingy expectations, and teach me to trust Your abundance. Make my hands open, my gratitude loud, and my table generous to others this day. Amen.

9:14.devotion: After exile, God promises to bring His people back to rebuild ruined cities, replant vineyards, and enjoy the fruit of their own gardens. It is a promise of ordinary, tangible life restored—homes, harvests, meals—reminding us that God's redemption touches the everyday work of our hands.
9:14.reflection: What broken or neglected part of my ordinary life do I need God to restore and rebuild?
9:14.action: Invest in one ordinary, life-giving task today—tending, building, or planting something that blesses your household.
9:14.prayer: Faithful God, You care about homes, harvests, and daily bread. Restore what has lain waste in my life, and bless the work of my hands so I may enjoy Your goodness and share it with those around me. Amen.

9:15.devotion: The book ends with God's firm word: He will plant His people in their land, never again to be uprooted. After chapters of warnings about exile, this final promise assures that the Lord's restoration is secure, rooted not in Israel's performance but in the covenant faithfulness of the LORD their God.
9:15.reflection: Do I trust that God's restoring grace holds firm, or do I fear He will give up on me?
9:15.action: Write down one promise of God you cling to and keep it where you will see it throughout the day.
9:15.prayer: Steadfast Lord, thank You that when You restore, You hold fast. Root me deep in Your love, so that when winds of fear or failure blow, I will not be uprooted but stand firm in You. Amen.
